schema_version: v0 — migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: Cast nodes — an intention that has passed /sorted, been typed to a node-class and bound to that class's gate-set. The universal work unit.
why: Workflow rides on node-class, not on the node's identity, so a ticket carries no domain — an 'inference ticket' and a 'concept-piece ticket' are the same artifact with a different class field. Everybody has tickets. Crucially, the ticket's `state` field IS the pipeline instance: no orchestrator holds a second copy of where the work stands, so the state of the tickets is the state of all things, always (MAP.md 'Gates, not supervisors'). Written when skill:/sorted casts a node.
owner: each ticket has exactly one owner who gates writes to it; the owner alone advances its state through the bound gates (Law 6). The tickets store owns the collection; the emit chokepoint validates records against the template.

template.owner: the one owner who gates writes to this node  ||  IN PRACTICE THIS FIELD RECORDS THE MOVER, NOT THE OWNER — measured 2026-08-10 across 91 filed tickets (5 distinct values name a component; the rest name a person, an agent, or a paragraph of prose). Under the ruling cited in `owning_intention` the owner of a ticket is its INTENTION, so this field's name and its contents disagree on most of the corpus. The disagreement is left standing deliberately: repairing 91 filed records is a fleet-wide change and it is filed as its own ticket, not smuggled in beside the read that noticed it.
template.owning_intention: the INTENTION that owns this ticket — an ADDRESS, resolved as a path to an `intention+why.json` (beside-code) or to a file under `intentions-not-beside-code/` (homeless), relative to either root. Ruled 2026-08-10 (decisions/2026-08-10-the-ticket-owns-the-refusal): 'the intentions always own their tickets' — and the chain runs on from here, an intention owns its TICKET, a ticket owns its WORKFLOW, and the workflow IS the boat, which is why `boat_id` has always been the ticket id. IT IS A NEW FIELD RATHER THAN A RE-READING OF EITHER NEIGHBOUR, and that is the whole point: `intention` above is the WHAT-prose and `owner` is, in practice, the MOVER. Measured over the 100 filed tickets on 2026-08-10: `intention` is present on 89 and 88 of those values run past 90 characters; `owner` is present on 91, only 5 distinct values name a component, and 56 run past 120. Both live up to their own declarations, so putting an address into either would be keeping a word and replacing what fills it — the exact failure that produced ticket boat-owner-is-read-not-stated. TELL THEM APART BY SHAPE, not by remembering which is which: this one RESOLVES as an address; the other two are prose. A PATH rather than a component roster name because the roster covers only the 24 beside-code intentions and homeless intentions have no roster name to give — a path is the one form every intention in the system can supply. NOT BACK-FILLED: a value nobody has checked is a translation with somebody's confidence attached, so the field grows against real gated crossings and its absence is what the gate REPORTS (by naming this file and the one-line fix) rather than what it guesses around.
template.intention: what this node is FOR (the WHAT)
template.node_class: the bound class (address in node_classes/): skill | concept-piece | code-seam | …
template.state: the pipeline instance — where this node is in its class's gate-set
template.gates: the class's gate-set bound at casting (proof / derivation / signature check-types)
template.falsifier: what would show this node wrong (required to cast)
template.parent: optional — parent node id (children prove before parents)
template.children: array — child node ids spawned to deconstruct this one
template.from_trouble: optional — the troubles/ id this ticket drains. REQUIRED if the ticket came from a trouble (Akien, ruling 2026-08-02: 'a TICKET that comes from a TROUBLE TICKET should say so'). Its presence is what makes the ticket P1.
template.priority: optional — 'P1' means an issue on the LIVE SYSTEM NOW. Every from_trouble ticket is P1 by default; a non-trouble ticket carries no priority unless it earns one.

entry.the_three_doors: IDEA (pre-intention design) → INTENT (/intent births and traces) → TICKET. This store is a DIRECT entry point, not only /sorted's output: a bug enters here without passing IDEA or INTENT.
entry.what_makes_it_structural_instead: LEVEL, not size or effort. Akien verbatim: 'if we have to edit lines of code to fix it, then it's not deeply structural... but if new information breaks the harmony of the system (eg an intention was implemented in a way contrary to the actual intention) with that version you and i have to reconcile it. that's structural.' A structural bug is reconciled with Akien; it does not enter here unexamined.
entry.why_the_test_is_shaped_this_way: The cost heuristic CC reaches for by default — big, scary, wide blast radius — is a judgment call, so it drifts. Akien's test names an OBSERVABLE: look at where the fix lands. Same move as intention+why.json forcing the why into the filename (Law 4 in miniature).

notes_on_the_store: TROUBLES DRAIN HERE. troubles/ is a pre-ticket inbox, not a parallel place work lives; a trouble that never becomes a ticket is a bug with no workflow. The trouble record stays (it is the account of the live symptom); the ticket is what moves through the gates.
A ticket is never terminal: `validated` = best guess still carrying its falsifier and horizon; the back-edge (build → deconstruct) is the universal shape.
A node with no falsifier does not cast (the /sorted completeness gate).
Ownership stays put; what moves phase-to-phase is which peer is invited to act next, through the owner's gate — not a transfer of ownership.
